roundShape: Full round, as the architect asked: 8f68d44d merges #2392 (the event horizon) through runtime files (event_stream_relay.go, live_events.go, delivery_live_hub*.go, server.go, store/pool.go), and 57c4a697 changes four hub-test rigs.

implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's suites at head. Events, outbox, store (on a fresh database) and multiprocess (129) pass. The api suite passes except two tests that are now flaky (failures below) and the local-collation test. The horizon claim holds on the real binary (proof below).

failures.criterion: No required test is made flaky by the change (the CI lanes that run internal/dispatch/api stay green).
failures.evidence: TestIdenticalViewsShareOneRecompute (delivery_live_hub_test.go:2086, 'recomputes for two identical views = 2, want 1') failed in CI's envoy-go-race-api at ed9b6759 (job 124369018657, log line 7697). Locally `go test -p 2 -parallel 4 ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestIdenticalViewsShareOneRecompute$' -count=20` fails 4 of 20 at head, and failed 2 of 15 in a second run. The same command at afab3fdc fails 0 of 15, and on main 76221977 fails 0 of 15. The extra recompute has cause=change: the relay feed, taken on a goroutine of the hub generation's own, marks every view dirty when it arrives. That is the seed recompute 57c4a697 settled in four other hub tests, and this test was not given the same settle.

failures.criterion: No required test is made flaky by the change (this PR's own held-lane order test).
failures.evidence: TestAHeldLaneKeepsItsQueuedCommentsInOrderThroughASweep fails 4 of 20 at head (`go test -p 2 -parallel 4 ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestAHeldLaneKeepsItsQueuedCommentsInOrderThroughASweep$' -count=20`), 3 of 15 in a second run, and once in the full api suite. The failure is 'the queued attempt of <id> for session:s1 does not carry the claim its sender holds' (comment_delivery_sender_test.go:954). The same command at afab3fdc fails 0 of 15. ageQueuedClaims holds sender.mu and expects each row's claimed_at to equal sender.claims. But the refresh loop (20 ms in this test) writes the rows outside the lock and updates the map afterwards under it (comment_mention_sender.go:340-350), so a refresh in flight leaves the row newer than the map. The merged pool change shifts the timing so the window is hit.

proof.criterion: The event horizon on the real binary: with an event insert held open below a committed comment, a live stream, a resume and an overflow catch-up each deliver both in id order once the insert commits, and none skips the lower id.
proof.surface: GET /ws/live, events view, as person-1 (wse client), against envoy-dispatch built from 859ac72d. The held insert is a psql transaction that calls pg_current_xact_id() and then inserts an artifact.version event, as Broker.Append does.
proof.command: horizon.sh live live; horizon.sh resume resume (reconnects with resume.since = the newest id before L); horizon2.sh head-stall (L1 held, 100 comments, L2 held, 100 comments with 3 KB bodies; the reader stops reading, with a 2 KB receive buffer, while L1 commits; Postgres logged every statement)
proof.observed: Live: nothing above L while it was open, then L (29786) and the comment (29787) in order. Resume: events_start replay_complete true and nothing until L committed, then 29786 and 29787. Overflow: after L1 committed the subscriber held 101 events, the highest 29886 = L2-1. Postgres logged two catch-up reads, 'id > 29850 and id <= 29886' and then 'id > 29951 and id <= 29987'. After L2 committed it held all 202 events once each, in id order, with L1 first and L2 at position 101. Past the replay bounds (300 comments of 6 KB): L and 64 events, then ended 'behind', as designed.
proof.negativeControl: The same three runs on round 16's build afab3fdc, whose relay reads past the horizon: live and resume deliver the comment while L is open, and L is never delivered. The overflow run delivers 200 events, and neither L1 nor L2 is ever delivered.

proof.criterion: Round 16's results still hold at this head: one frame per mention, the late-answered Retry leaves one copy, the restart without a storm.
proof.surface: Go tests through go -overlay; two Dispatch processes with slowsend.py in front of the second process's listener; the load-test restart scenario
proof.command: go test -overlay ov/head.json and ov/modekey.json -run 'TestR8|TestRepro'; timedretry.sh h17-none none and h17-route route; run-step.sh r17-restart-1x --events 4 --sessions 400 --requests 60 --live 50 --live-resume 1 --live-stale 10 --restart-at 90s --mention-frac 0.2 --mentions 3 --envoy-rtt 200ms
proof.observed: The r8 repro hands 1 frame. The late-answered Retry: attempt 1 is sent with duplicate=true, ses-y stores one copy and nothing stays pending, with and without a route. Restart (build 859ac72d, clean tree): 50 reconnects, replayed frames per reconnect at most 35 (last_id) and 9 (stale, 12,600 behind), 10 refetches by the stale sockets, 898 KiB replayed in total, 19.5 Dispatch CPU-s in the minute after the restart. Sampled pod memory peak during it: 7.6 GB.
proof.negativeControl: With the mode restored in the key, the r8 repro hands 2 frames and fails.

proof.criterion: The migration runs both ways against main; the hub-test rig change only waits for the seed.
proof.surface: A scratch database 'mig'; the diff of 57c4a697
proof.command: mig.sh main, head, main, head on database mig (main is 76221977, which carries 0149_event_horizon); jj diff -r 57c4a697
proof.observed: Main migrates a fresh database to 149, head applies 150 (comment_fallback_copies and its 2 indexes), main starts healthy on the 150 database, and head starts again. 57c4a697 adds rig.settle() waits, narrows the held-recompute filter to the measured timeline view, subscribes a warm measures view before the measured timeline, raises one wait from 3 s to eventFeedWait (30 s), and adds one freshness expectation. No assertion is removed or loosened. The warm view does mean the timeline is no longer the generation's first view in that test.
